recommendations.title: Erstellung eines Verletzungsregisters im Profifusball - Studiendesign und Perspektiven
recommendations.authors: Szymski D., Krutsch W., Huber L., Weber J. and Alt V.
recommendations.reason: The verified corresponding full report describes prospective national injury and illness registries for the German men's and women's professional first and second Bundesliga. Team medical staff prospectively report time-loss outcomes and the paper publishes match-exposure incidence rates.
recommendations.dataCollectionTiming: Men's registry introduced in 2022/2023 and women's registry in 2023/2024, with monthly team-medical-staff reporting and longitudinal follow-up.
recommendations.populationEligibility: Professional male and female football players in the German first and second Bundesliga (1,514 players from 54 teams in the first season).
recommendations.competitionContext: German professional men's and women's first and second Bundesliga league competitions and training.
recommendations.dataSource: Prospective REDCap registries completed by team medical staff, with official match statistics for exposure data.
recommendations.outcomeEligibility: Time-loss injuries, illnesses, injury incidence and return-to-play duration.
recommendations.injuryIllnessDefinition: All time-loss injuries and illnesses reported with standardised electronic forms, adapted from established football and IOC surveillance protocols; return to play is medical clearance for full team training and match play.
recommendations.reportedDenominator: Published injury incidence per 1,000 hours of match exposure, including 3.16 for male ankle sprain and 2.56 for female ankle sprain.
recommendations.denominatorEvidenceQuote: The most frequent injury in male professional football in Germany was ankle sprains with an incidence of 3.16 per 1000 hours match exposure and a mean time-loss of 7.3 days.
evidenceQuotes: Methods Two prospective registries were introduced in the first and second divisions of German professional football (men: 2022/2023, women: 2023/2024). Team medical staff reported all time-loss injuries and illnesses using a standardised, pseudonymised protocol on an online platform.
Match exposure data were obtained directly from official match statistics for all players. Injury and illness match incidence rates were calculated per 1000 hours of match exposure.
The most frequent injury in male professional football in Germany was ankle sprains with an incidence of 3.16 per 1000 hours match exposure and a mean time-loss of 7.3 days.
During the first season, 1185 time-loss events were recorded (men: 503 injuries, 176 illnesses; women: 362 injuries, 144 illnesses).

identityEvidence: The final-pass manifest confirms that all five conference-record authors recur in the full report.

The original record's first male-season counts, 503 injuries and 176 illnesses, are reproduced in the full report; the later report additionally includes the women's cohort.
Both records describe monthly physician reporting, standardised forms, a time-loss definition and longitudinal registry design.
